q: Can kiln or cooler exhaust heat replace dryer fuel, and how do I count it?
title: Kiln exhaust heat for dryers
short: Yes, ducting hot air from a kiln's cooling zone or exhaust to a dryer can replace some dryer fuel. Count the saving as lower fuel on the dryer's own bills or meter. Do not add a separate credit for the recovered heat; it is already inside the kiln's fuel.
audience: Ceramic, brick, refractory and food processing plants

ul: Tile and sanitaryware kilns feeding body or glaze dryers.
Cement or lime cooler air feeding raw material drying.
Biscuit and snack ovens feeding pre-dryers.

ol: Measure dryer fuel per tonne for a few months before.
Measure again after the duct is in service, at similar output.
Multiply the fuel saved by its factor. Fan electricity added is Scope 2.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
